title: Chinese Republicans by Alex Lin at Roundabout #chineserepublicans #ro...
transcript: This play frustrated me because I really wanted to like it, but I don't think it's there yet. Chinese Republicans is a new play about four women in an affinity group at their corporate finance firm. When the youngest member, starry-eyed 24-year-old Katie, gets a rude awakening, it threatens the optics of the whole group. Described as a “bitingly funny satire” about capitalism, assimilation, and gender politics, I didn't find it very satirical, except for the unrealistic plot that goes pretty far off the rails. It's actually pretty serious, with references to citizenship-related threats, workplace SA, and discrimination. Now, I'm not saying you can't use a humorous vehicle to convey serious ideas, but the tone isn't clear enough yet so things feel misaligned. The most unhinged and offensive moments here are definitely the funniest, but they aren't properly leveraged or integrated into the message of the piece in a meaningful way. As it stands, I think there might be two great plays incubating within this one, I'm just not sure how well they do together. But I sincerely hope this production finds more of a footing throughout the rest of its previews — it doesn't yet do justice to its four great AAPI actresses and its genuinely insightful set of ideas. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
